questions.q: According to this lesson, what does 'orchestration' actually mean?
options: Defining tasks, their order, their schedule, and failure handling as a first-class, inspectable system
Writing a single Python script with no structure
Manually running each step by hand every day
A synonym for writing SQL queries
questions.explain: Orchestration treats task order, scheduling, and failure handling as explicit, inspectable concerns — not something buried inside a script's control flow.

options: An open-source orchestration platform where pipelines are defined as Python code (DAGs)
A SQL database engine
A BI/reporting tool like Power BI
A programming language
questions.explain: Airflow lets you define pipelines as Python code and handles scheduling, tracking, and retries for you.

questions.q: Where does this course sit relative to dbt and Snowflake in the Analytics Engineer path, and why?
options: Right after both — dbt models the data, Snowflake stores it, and Airflow triggers the whole pipeline on a schedule
Before both — Airflow must be learned before any SQL
Airflow replaces the need for dbt and Snowflake entirely
There is no relationship between the three tools
questions.explain: Airflow is the orchestration layer that ties together tools like dbt and Snowflake — it makes sense to learn it after knowing what it's actually coordinating.

questions.q: In Airflow's UI run-history grid, what does a red cell mean?
options: That specific task failed on that specific run
The entire Airflow installation crashed
A task is scheduled but hasn't started yet
Nothing — colors are purely decorative
questions.explain: Each cell represents one task on one run; red means that specific task failed on that specific run.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the biggest practical difference between Airflow and a cron job with no visibility?
options: When something fails, you look at the UI and know immediately which task and run failed, rather than SSHing in and grepping logs
Airflow never fails, unlike cron jobs
Cron jobs are always faster than Airflow
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: Airflow's UI gives immediate, inspectable visibility into exactly what happened, replacing the need to manually dig through server logs.
